claims.text: The starting material is cast and homogenized equiatomic NbMoTaW with an average grain size of approximately 20 µm and no boron doping.
Adding approximately 0.1 at% interstitial boron will significantly improve the room-temperature ductility of equiatomic NbMoTaW.
Boron will segregate to grain boundaries in NbMoTaW.
Grain-boundary boron segregation will reduce the propensity for intergranular fracture.
Interstitial boron lowers grain-boundary energy and enhances grain-boundary cohesion.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion facilitates dislocation transmission across boundaries at room temperature.
Improved dislocation transmission promotes more uniform room-temperature plastic flow and greater ductility.
At 1600 °C, boron remains in solid solution without forming gross precipitates.
The absence of gross boron-rich precipitates preserves the alloy's high-temperature strength and creep behavior.
Under irradiation, boron clusters act as defect sinks.
Boron clusters acting as defect sinks maintain swelling and irradiation-hardening behavior near the undoped baseline.
Room-temperature total elongation will increase from less than 1% to approximately 5–10%.
The 1600 °C yield strength of boron-doped NbMoTaW will remain within ±10% of the undoped baseline of approximately 400–500 MPa.
Irradiation-induced swelling and hardness changes in boron-doped NbMoTaW will remain within ±5% of the undoped baseline.
Undoped NbMoTaW has room-temperature elongation below 1%.
Undoped NbMoTaW has a 1600 °C yield strength of approximately 450 MPa.
Undoped NbMoTaW exhibits negligible swelling after 10 dpa Kr ion irradiation.
The hypothesis is restricted to 0.05–0.2 at% boron, grain sizes of 10–50 µm, no detectable boron-rich second phases, and irradiation temperatures no higher than 600 °C.
Boron contents above approximately 0.2 at% create a risk of boride formation.
